maya: quick design review — draft for the capacity confirmation modal. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/XYZ/capacity-confirmation (copy + states) liam: skimmed — overall 🙌. one flag: the cost line feels vague. sara: agree. suggest changing 'estimated cost impact' -> 'estimated monthly cost change' and show a small tooltip for assumptions. ethan: accessibility note: when modal opens focus should go to the first actionable element (probably the main CTA). also need aria-live for the cost estimate updates. olivia: small product ask: include a one-line 'why this matters' under the header to call out SLO/latency impact. maya: updated figma with that line. question: should CTA say "Apply changes" or "Confirm and provision"? liam: "Confirm and provision" is clearer about the action (spinning up capacity), but might feel heavy for small edits. sara: microcopy vote: "Apply changes" + secondary note under CTA "provisions capacity in ~2 minutes" — keeps primary short. ben: GPU pool selector: we should show pool badges (GPUs available / avg latency tier) in the modal so people can choose without going back to the pool page. olivia: +1 for badges. also highlight which pool will be used for burst capacity so it's obvious when burst is enabled. ethan: keyboard/assistive tech details: focus trap inside modal, close on ESC, ensure form errors are announced via aria-live. sample snippet: ```html
Estimated monthly cost: $12.34
``` maya: thanks. UX question: if user sets min == max, should burst be disabled or allowed but ignored? liam: edge-case: if min==max and burst enabled leads to transient scaling surprises. probably better to disable burst toggle and show tooltip explaining why. sara: wording suggestion for tooltip: "Burst requires min < max. Enable burst to allow short-term capacity spikes without increasing baseline cost." ben: also show an inline guardrail: "Projected peak QPS with burst: 1200 (estimated)" — helps folks understand impact. olivia: can we surface an estimated SLO effect: "99p latency expected: 120ms -> 95ms"? curious if we can compute safely without overpromising. maya: product decision needed. maybe show relative delta with clear "estimate" label. we should not show guarantees. liam: visuals: prefer a condensed summary row at top of modal with three columns: cost delta, SLO delta, pool chosen. then details below expandable. sara: accessibility nits: ensure contrast ratios of badges meet AA, and icon-only controls have aria-labels. also increase hit target of the burst toggle to 44px. ben: implementation note: when user changes min/max sliders, we should debounce estimate requests (250ms) and show skeleton while computing. ethan: also expose option to view the raw assumptions (sequence length, tokens/hr) behind cost estimate in a small link "assumptions" that opens a lightweight panel. maya: updated action items in the figma comments. deploy-bot: image uploaded -> screenshot_02.png deploy-bot: uploaded screenshot_02.png to #product (preview) sara: quick copy tweak for disabled-burst tooltip: change 'requires min < max' -> 'requires min to be lower than max' (reads better). liam: tiny UX gripe: primary CTA color currently same as danger in dark theme. pls check states across themes. maya: noted. final asks: - implement focus/aria changes - add pool badges and burst-disabled state - microcopy edits (sara's suggestions) - debounce + skeleton - top summary row + expandable details olivia: i'll prep a short product spec for engineering with measurable acceptance criteria. ben: i'll sketch a compact layout for the badges so it fits mobile widths. maya: thanks everyone — follow-ups in figma comments and I'll ping next Tuesday for the final sign-off. :thumbsup:
